issues.description: Identity seed/increment grammar accepts signed numbers but the value is no longer a single value
issues.detail: SignedSegmentGrammar is now an optional sibling of NumericLiteralSegment rather than part of one signed-numeric value. A downstream consumer reading the IDENTITY seed must now reassemble sign+magnitude from two adjacent nodes instead of receiving one signed number. Value and its sign have been complected across two grammar slots; prefer a SignedNumericLiteralSegment so a seed remains one value.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE now accepts NumericLiteralSegment with no justification or test
issues.detail: The grammar widened from QuotedLiteral to also permit NakedIdentifier and NumericLiteral, but the added test only exercises the identifier form (us_english). A numeric language id is a different fact about the world (lcid vs name); admitting it without a fixture is speculative scope and leaves the parse shape under-specified. Either cite the docs and add a test, or drop the numeric branch.

issues.description: ALTER TABLE refactor from Delimited(OneOf(...)) to bare OneOf silently drops comma-separated mixed clauses
issues.detail: The prior shape allowed multiple heterogeneous alter actions in one statement; the new shape only allows one action per ALTER TABLE, with delimitation pushed inside DROP COLUMN/CONSTRAINT. The deleted fixture (ADD column_b ... , DROP COLUMN column_a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS column_c) was valid TSQL and is now unparseable. That is a real semantic narrowing dressed as a refactor; call it out or restore it.

issues.description: DROP CONSTRAINT inner Sequence wraps an optional Sequence that itself contains another optional
issues.detail: The DROP CONSTRAINT branch nests Sequence(Sequence('CONSTRAINT', IfExists, optional=True), ObjectReference) inside a Delimited. Two layers of optional Sequence around two keywords is incidental nesting; a flatter Sequence with Ref('CONSTRAINT', optional=True) and Ref('IfExistsGrammar', optional=True) expresses the same grammar with one fewer level. Small, but the shape will read in the YAML forever.

review.summary: The PR adds four narrow TSQL parser extensions and is mostly mechanical, but two changes complect concerns that should stay separate. The identity seed/increment now represents a signed number as two sibling grammar nodes instead of one value, pushing sign reassembly onto every consumer. The ALTER TABLE rewrite is presented as a refactor but actually narrows the accepted grammar and deletes a previously-valid fixture without saying so. DEFAULT_LANGUAGE widens to numerics with no fixture or citation. Decomplect the signed literal, name the ALTER TABLE narrowing explicitly, and either justify the numeric language branch with a test or drop it.
